attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: A flat, categorical observation of zero exits and zero IPOs. In context it means generative AI startups over roughly the prior three years. The normalisation matches it.

contract.note: On a plain reading, an exit includes acquisition of an operating business. The speaker's own post lists acquisitions, so this reading is not stretched against him. A single completed qualifying acquisition defeats the zero claim.

evidence.note: Wix's own disclosure confirms it acquired Base44, an AI app-building product business. The packet's cross-check dates the deal to June 2025, before the post. This is a qualifying exit not acknowledged in the post.

Canva's completed acquisition of Leonardo.ai (July 2024, cash and stock, ongoing business) is a qualifying exit within the period. That the speaker mentions it elsewhere does not save the categorical sentence.

reviews.rationale: The sentence says there were no exits at all. Completed acquisitions of operating generative AI businesses happened within the period: Leonardo.ai by Canva in 2024 and Base44 by Wix in mid-2025. The IPO half is not established either way, but the combined zero-event claim is false.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The drafter's 'unlikely' softens a firm statement ('I just don't see how'), which the context backs with 'I expect'. The proposition also bundles in a separate, unmeasurable claim that Anthropic depends on Cursor. The scorable core is a firm forecast that Cursor will neither survive nor get a conventional exit.

contract.note: The speaker's own test was an actual sale of $10B or more, not an acqui-hire. A $60B whole-company merger meets that test plainly, so the contract is fair. The Anthropic-dependence part has no threshold and stays unscored.

evidence.note: Cursor's own announcement, dated 2026-08-14, says the acquisition by SpaceX is complete. This is a company disclosure, corroborated by e2.
Reporting on the closing filing says the merger took effect August 14, 2026, making Anysphere a wholly owned SpaceX subsidiary. It was all-stock at a $60B implied value: a full transfer of ownership.

reviews.rationale: The forecast had no deadline, but the early-resolution rule was met by a dated event. SpaceX completed its acquisition of Cursor as a whole business in August 2026, at a value far above the speaker's own $10B bar. The business survived and exited. The separate claim that Anthropic depends on Cursor has no threshold and remains unresolved.

semantics.note: The revised normalisation keeps 'seem', 'almost entirely', 'bizarre' and 'confusing'. The central description is hedged with 'seem', and 'sparse' names no comparison group.

contract.note: The contract treats 'seem' as non-binding and scores the description as firm. Policy says hedged language is not scored. It also has to invent a comparison group and an 'overwhelming predominance' standard the speaker never gave.

evidence.note: The UK CMA page confirms Microsoft–Inflection was a hiring-based arrangement: one example, no market share. It is labelled company_disclosure but is actually a regulator's record.
Canva's announcement shows Leonardo continuing as an independent business. It is one counterexample, but the speaker himself lists it, and 'almost entirely' allows exceptions.
Databricks completed its MosaicML acquisition in 2023 with the product continuing. It is one example and may fall outside his applications-only scope; it gives no proportions.

reviews.rationale: The central description is hedged with 'seem' and loaded with subjective words ('bizarre', 'confusing'). 'Sparse' has no comparison group. The packet has no representative list of deals, and its few examples cannot establish or refute the overall proportions. As stated, the claim cannot be scored.

semantics.note: 'Will, I believe' is a firm expectation, not a probability, so this is a scorable forecast. It has no deadline and no numeric threshold, and the weekly limits are its antecedent.

contract.note: A plain reading (historically exceptional paid churn caused by the limits) is fair. The contract rightly requires representative churn data, not complaints or net growth figures.

evidence.note: Shows weekly limits were in force by March 2026, so the antecedent is met. It says nothing about churn, so it is not evidence of the outcome.
A self-selected GitHub thread with stated intentions to cancel and one resubscription. It gives no churn rate for the population.
Anthropic's own disclosure of growth in Claude Code users and revenue. Net growth can hide cancellations, so it does not measure churn.

reviews.rationale: The weekly limits were introduced, so the antecedent is met. But the forecast has no deadline, and the packet has no representative churn data and no comparison with historical SaaS churn. Anecdotes and company growth figures do not meet the early-resolution rule, so the forecast stays open.
